system.summary: The main system: one- and two-digit codes with no spaces; a and o each have two codes; code 74 is che; code 36 is read as a null. The earlier system (R4034 to R4038) uses the archive's key table R4033, with letter codes and word signs.
system.notes: distinct_symbols counts the code types of key/key-main.tsv (the main system). The nomenclator has 69 entries: code 74 (che) of the main key, and the 68 word signs of the archive's table (names, titles and common words). Diacritics: a bar over the digits marks a word sign of the earlier system; the main system has none.

prior_solution.where: No earlier decipherment of these letters is known to me. The archive's key table R4033 is a key of the earlier system, not a decipherment. Ferrai (1882), p. 136, note 1, prints the wording of a sister letter of R4054, not R4054.

texts.label: R4034, Cosimo I to Niccolini, 17 December 1537
texts.summary: My words, a paraphrase of the reading: The tithes. Cosimo writes that he begged someone not to burden a party, at present so exhausted, with such a levy; the code for that party has no value. His Majesty's aid is named. A doubtful word sign that the table gives as the Emperor stands at four places: his favour, his mind, his coming near Italy. After "il prefat", a doubtful barred sign gives the table's King of France; cut otherwise, it gives "Arciuescouo" (archbishop). Niccolini is to draw the matter out as long as he can, with no offer, because time can bring much advantage. The passage probably names the case of "Altopaso" (perhaps Altopascio).
texts.note: Reading in sentences and English translation on the record page, made from the decode. Counts by the word rule (an estimate): 112 cipher words, 77 sure, 35 holes; read share 0.688. Under the read bar; 0 of 8 sentences and fragments have at most one hole in ten words. README.md.
reading: [M]olto caldamente che fusi con [lui], e suplicavolo per parte di quelo, che fusi contento non molestare [4̅7̅] di presente tanto exausto con tale exatione.
Il prefat[o] Re di Fra[n]za e
Di Sua Maestà lo aiuto & [fa]vore del Imper[ato]re più in lungo che potrete, senza venire a oferta alcuna.

O esendosi avi[c]inato l'Imper[ato]re a Italia, m[e]tere tempo in mezo & tirare la cosa più in lungo che si può, perche il tempo ci può porta[r]e [53] molta comodità … esendo la mente del Imper[ato]re tale … non solo sopra q[u]esta cosa dele decime, ma sopra la causa di {Altopaso}.
translation: [Very] [earnestly] that I should be with [him], and I was begging him on behalf of that one, that he should be content not to trouble [...], at present [so] exhausted, with such an exaction.
His Majesty's aid and the [Emperor]'s [favour] for as [long] as you can, without coming to any offer.

Or, [the] [Emperor] having [drawn near] to Italy, [to put] time in between and draw the matter out as long [as] one can, because time can [bring] us [...] much advantage … the [Emperor]'s mind [being] such … not only on [this] [matter] [of the] [tithes] [but] on [the] case of {Altopaso}.

texts.label: R4035, Cosimo I to Niccolini, 24 December 1537
texts.summary: My words, a paraphrase of the reading: The passage names those who have grown and fattened on the ruin of others and on ours, and His Holiness doing worse to this city and state. It ends: "to proceed in this business as the Prince will do at Genoa".
texts.note: Reading in sentences and English translation on the record page, made from the decode. Counts by the word rule (an estimate): 29 cipher words, 26 sure, 3 holes; read share 0.897. If code 29 = t, from ciphertext, does not count as given by the key: 17 sure, 12 holes (0.586). Under the read bar; 1 of 2 sentences and fragments have at most one hole in ten words. README.md.
reading: Crescuti & ingrasati delle rovine delli altri, de[l]e nostre, [c]he Sua Santità faci pegio a qu[e]sta cità & stato.
Procedere in questo negotio come farà il Principe a Genova.
translation: Grown and fattened on the ruins of others, [on] ours, [that] His Holiness should do worse to [this] city and state.
To proceed in this business as the Prince will in Genoa.

texts.label: R4036, Cosimo I to Niccolini, 8 February 1538

texts.note: Reading in sentences and English translation on the record page, made from the decode. Counts by the word rule (an estimate): 12 cipher words, 1 sure, 11 holes; read share 0.083. Under the read bar; 0 of 2 sentences and fragments have at most one hole in ten words. README.md.
reading: Se ve[n]ga bisog[n]o, and[r]ò [a] fermare a dieci {mi[la]}.

texts.label: R4037, Cosimo I to Niccolini, 16 February 1538
texts.summary: My words, a paraphrase of the reading: The two papal tithes on Florence. Cosimo writes that he was given to understand that he should proceed in this business as he sees "the prince … Doria" and the city of Genoa proceed. A proposal: to be content with half of the two tithes, one raised now and one a year later, by a Florentine commissioner whom His Holiness appoints. Church censures and an interdict are named.
texts.note: Reading in sentences and English translation on the record page, made from the decode. Counts by the word rule (an estimate): 243 cipher words, 201 sure, 42 holes; read share 0.827. If code 29 = t, from ciphertext, does not count as given by the key: 159 sure, 84 holes (0.654). Under the read bar; 1 of 7 sentences and fragments have at most one hole in ten words. README.md.
reading: Ala corte del [...] per ordine di quelo & di queli sua consiglieri mi è st[at]o fato in[t][e]ndere che in questo negotio dele [d]ecime io mi governi & proceda in quel modo me[d]esimo che io vederò governarsi & proce[d]ere al princip[e]… Doria & ala cità di Genova.

Il deto signore princ[i]pe & quela cità non sono ven[u]ti con [...] ad acordo o co[m][po]sitione alcuna … haveva dele al[t]re dificultà & cose di più importantia da resolvere con [...] dele dec[i]me nostre di qua, ma che tuto proceda dala dureza de [...], dove va lo interese del denaro.
Qualche re[s]peto & consideratione a me non nota, di gravare & stringere [...], al Marchese cioè, & del ordine & comisione che io tengo in questa parte dal [...].

Contentarsi de [l]a metà di le due decime da exigersi l'u[na] di presente & l'altra di qui a uno ano, per uno comisario fiorentino deputato da l[a] Sua Santità per magiore iustificatione & scarico del animo suo … del deto comisario, un[o] suo fidato.

& se {le} procederà ale censure & interdeti, ce ne dorà e[t] hare[m]o patientia. La cità è stata interdeta con qualche più colore, & questa sia la ultima resolutione. Si acet[e]rano le due decime poste da [...], una dele quali habia [a] esere … [pe]r quela, l'altra per la cità … da exigersi per comi[ss]arii fiorentini, quanto al ordine & … [c]omisione che io tengo dala corte del [...].
translation: At the court [of the] [...], by order of [that one] and of those counsellors of his, I [was] made [to understand] that in this business of the [tithes] I should conduct myself and proceed in the [same] way that I shall see the [Prince] … Doria and the city of Genoa conduct themselves and [proceed].

The said lord [Prince] and that city have not [come] to any agreement or [settlement] with [...] … he had [other] difficulties and things of greater importance to resolve with [...] about our [tithes] here, but that it all proceeds from the hardness of [...], where the interest of the money lies.
Some [regard] and consideration unknown to me, of burdening and pressing [...], to the Marquis, that is, and of the order and commission that I hold in this matter from the [...].

To be content with [the] half of the two tithes to be collected, the [one] at present and [the] [other] a year from now, by a Florentine commissioner deputed by [the] His Holiness for greater justification and relief of his conscience … of the said commissioner, [a] trusted one of his.

And if {she} proceeds to censures and interdicts, it will grieve us [and] [we shall have] patience. The city has been put under interdict with somewhat more pretext, and let this be the final resolution. The two tithes imposed by [...] [will be accepted], one of which is [to] be … [for] that one, the other for the city … to be collected by Florentine [commissioners], as to the order and … [commission] that I hold from the court of the [...].

texts.label: R4038, Cosimo I to Niccolini, 4 March 1538
texts.summary: My words, a paraphrase of the reading: Niccolini is to accept the extension "se[c]ondo Clemente" (perhaps "as under Pope Clement"), as they have said, and have it issued as in the copy that is sent to him. If they knew of it, they would not want it so broad, or would want better terms. Any further advantage is left to him.
texts.note: Reading in sentences and English translation on the record page, made from the decode. Counts by the word rule (an estimate): 50 cipher words, 41 sure, 9 holes; read share 0.820. Under the read bar; 0 of 2 sentences and fragments have at most one hole in ten words. README.md.
reading: Ad[ve]…rtendo Vostra Signor[i]a che aceti la estensione, se[c]ondo Clemente come loro hano deto, & poi si espedisca confor[m]e ala co[p]ia che se li manda, perche quando ne havesino notitia, o non la voriano così ampla o con meglio condit[i]one. Inoltre, potendosi vantag[i]are in cosa alcuna, lo rimetiamo in lei.
translation: [Ad…vising] Your [Lordship] to accept the extension [according to] Clement, as they have said, and then let it be issued [in accordance] with the [copy] that is sent to you, because if they had notice of it, they would either not want it so broad or would want it on better [terms]. Furthermore, if [advantage] can be [gained] in [any] thing, we leave it to you.

texts.label: R4039, Cosimo I to Niccolini, 4 October 1538
texts.summary: Cosimo writes about a marriage alliance and "the matter of the wife". His intention in the matter of the wife has always been the same, from the start until now. He encloses a copy of a letter. Its aim is to cut off this negotiation entirely, because it is too contrary to his mind. He warns Niccolini about one man. That man is not to be trusted, and he fears to lose "his penitentiary" (an office). The same man acted against Duke Alessandro "of good memory", and against Cosimo at his arrival.
texts.note: Counts by the word rule (an estimate): 321 cipher words, 188 sure, 133 holes; read share 0.586. README.md.

texts.label: R4047, Cosimo I to Niccolini, 18 January 1539
texts.summary: Cosimo writes about a "motu proprio" (an act that the pope issues on his own initiative) and about how to use it. The matter "would turn to our great advantage, more than theirs". He hopes that they will do it, and he says that it is right to act "at the right time and place". He wants to make them feel "a great suspicion". When "this fear" is taken away, "another suspicion" stays "in this cause".

texts.label: R4054, Cosimo I to Niccolini, 11 August 1539
texts.summary: Cosimo writes about the arrest of one Biagio della Campana. The passage also names Giulio, the natural son of Duke Alessandro. Biagio della Campana had always kept company with "the sons of Bartolomeo Valori". He was taken two years before and examined. Many crimes were found in him, which deserved every punishment. A sentence of the Balìa condemned him, and he was sent to the fortress of Pisa. Later he was freed, with many other prisoners.
texts.note: Counts by the word rule (an estimate): 179 cipher words, 92 sure, 87 holes; read share 0.514. README.md.
